reason: The mechanism exists but both load-bearing measurements are wrong, and the consequence built on them does not happen. (1) THE SCROLL JUMP IS NOT THE HREF'S. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?v=light&state=full: the document scroller is 1644px tall against a 960px viewport, so maxScroll is exactly 684 — the seat's y=684 is the very bottom of the page — and .tabs sits at document y=78..122. At scrollY=684 the strip's rect is top -606 / bottom -562: entirely off-screen and unclickable. Focusing 'Today's Signal' at that scroll position scrolls it into view on its own; measured scrollY immediately AFTER .focus() and BEFORE any Enter is 0. So 'pressing Enter sets scrollY to 0' is false as attributed — scrollY was already 0 when the key was pressed, and deleting the href would not change that. Shift+Tab reaches the strip the same way. The real, reproducible jump is bounded by where the strip lives: clicking a tab at scrollY=100 lands at 0, a 100px snap, and no click is possible above ~122px because the strip has scrolled away. A ~120px maximum, not 684. (2) IT IS NOT ONE BACK PRESS PER ACTIVATION. Measured from a fresh load, clicking tab 1, 2, 3, then 1 again: history.length goes 2 -> 3 -> 3 -> 3 -> 3, hash '' throughout after the first. The empty fragment is pushed exactly once; every subsequent activation is a same-URL fragment navigation and pushes nothing. The claimed consequence — 'silently spends one Back press per attempt... three tries and their Back button appears broken, they press it three times' — is not what the browser does. It is one stray entry, ever, no matter how many times the strip is pressed, and one Back press restores the clean URL. (3) The press-state half is accurate but re-files a closed decision. Confirmed: siblings measure rgb(113,113,122) rest -> rgb(17,17,17) hover -> rgb(17,17,17) held; the aria-current tab measures rgb(17,17,17) at all three. But a tab that is already the current page is not an actionable control, and every benchmark named in the brief (Linear, Stripe, Vercel) leaves the selected tab inert under hover and press. The absence of a tab press state was settled by no-pressed-state-anywhere (r1): interaction-check.mjs:1316-1340 fixes the press roster at .btn and .dot and states in comment which objects were retired from it. No regression is cited and none was measured. (4) The severity is overstated by two classes. Nothing is blocking, nothing asserts anything untrue, and nothing is visibly wrong to a reader: a trailing '#' and a <=120px snap on a click made in the top 122px of the document. That is a refinement. (5) The round-2 precedent cited is not the same object. kpi-cards-are-links-that-open-nothing was an invented affordance with no destination anywhere, so the role was removed. The tab strip is locked architecture whose two siblings have real routes (/app/home and /app/home/briefing); their '#' is a prototype stand-in for a route, and the seat's own fix concedes it must be swapped for the real hrefs on the port packet. Blanket-guarding the strip in the master would encode the placeholder as the design.
sharpenedFix: Do not guard all three tabs. The only durable one-liner is the self-link on the tab that is already current, which has nowhere to go in the prototype or in the shipped app: after the [data-tip] listener loop in lately.html (~line 1212) add `const cur = root.querySelector('.tab[aria-current=\"page\"]'); if (cur) cur.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.preventDefault());`. That removes the one stray history entry and the snap without touching the two tabs that will carry real routes — and it survives the port, because a current tab must not re-navigate to itself. The two siblings should keep an href and get their real routes on the port packet; guarding them now trades a stray fragment for a tab that visibly does nothing, which is the worse of the two. Leave the press states alone: a selected tab that does not react to a press is correct, not missing.
breaks: The current-tab guard breaks nothing on this surface — the anchor keeps its role, its focus-visible ring, its 600 weight and its ::after underline, and no gate assertion reads .tab click behaviour. Two things to re-measure if it lands: interaction-check.mjs:1051 (the tab strip naming assertion) still passes, and the focus order Tab-1/2/3 -> .dot is unchanged, since preventDefault does not affect focusability. If the broad version in the finding were taken instead, re-measure the port: the selector `.tab` would have to be narrowed by hand when the two routes are wired, or both siblings would ship as dead links — the exact failure the KPI-card fix was meant to end.
